title: Robo2Process: Benchmarking and Learning Process-Aware Understanding in Vision-Language Robotic Manipulation
claim: A benchmark and data pipeline are presented as a unified system, with a grid of task families spanning two reasoning categories.
layout: Top pipeline strip left-to-right; below, two-section grid of 12 task cards
description: The top band shows a left-to-right pipeline. First, source inputs: language commands in speech bubbles, gripper-force and contact signal plots, and a filmstrip of manipulation video with primitive labels. Big orange arrows lead to a Local Process Units segmentation block (Start, LPU1..N, End, stable regime filtering, contact identification, motion detection, subtask labels, signal alignment). Next comes a ProcessData-58k box (12 tasks, 260 questions, human verified), then a finetuning block for Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL3-8B. The center has a dashed RoboProcessBench logo box. The bottom half is split into a blue Static Monitoring section and an orange Dynamic Reasoning section. Together they hold 12 cards (T1–T12). Each card has a robot photo, a short question and a green-checked answer.
caption: Overview of Robo2Process and RoboProcessBench. Robo2Process converts source-native execution traces into local process units and structured QA supervision. RoboProcessBench instantiates 12 question families across static monitoring and dynamic reasoning.
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) used as robotic critics, reward generators, and failure detectors must understand how manipulation unfolds, not only whether it succeeds. Yet fine-grained process supervision is not readily available in a unified form, and existing evaluations do not systematically diagnose these abilities. We introduce Robo2Process, a trace-grounded framework for scalable construction of process-aware supervision from heterogeneous robotic execution data. It aligns visual observations with source-native signals and annotations, extracts local process units (LPUs), and generates structured QA supervision through task-specific sampling, deterministic label construction, and ambiguity filtering. We instantiate this framework as RoboProcessBench, a diagnostic benchmark with 12 question families spanning \emph{static monitoring} and \emph{dynamic reasoning}, and ProcessData, a corpus of 57,892 QA pairs across four data sources and 260 manipulation tasks, split into ProcessData-SFT and ProcessData-Eval. Evaluation of a broad suite of VLMs reveals uneven process understanding. Supervision from ProcessData-SFT improves \textit{Qwen2.5-VL-7B} and \textit{InternVL-3-8B} on local state, motion, progress, and primitive-aware cues. External evaluation on RoboRewardBench shows Robo2Process enables out-of-distribution process-aware reasoning abilities. Overall, Robo2Process provides a source-aware pipeline, diagnostic benchmark, and learnable substrate for process-aware understanding in robotic manipulation.
